# Lab 6.5: Read the Query Execution Graph

## What We Are Going to Do
Run a heavier query and use the execution graph to find the slowest stage, shuffle size and any spills.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Run a join and aggregation.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT t.company, COUNT(*) AS trips, ROUND(AVG(t.fare), 2) AS avg_fare,
       COUNT(DISTINCT t.taxi_id) AS taxis
FROM lab06.trips_flat t
JOIN (SELECT company, COUNT(*) AS c FROM lab06.trips_flat GROUP BY company HAVING c &gt; 1000) big
  USING (company)
GROUP BY t.company
ORDER BY trips DESC;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] Open the Execution graph.** For each stage look at:
   - **Stage name** (Input, Join, Aggregate, Output)
   - **Records read / written**
   - **Slot time** and **wait / read / compute / write** split
   - **Shuffle output bytes** and **spilled** bytes

   Click the stage with the largest **Slot time**. That is where the work is.

3. **[Console] Compare slot time and elapsed time.** In **Job information**, **Slot milliseconds** divided by elapsed milliseconds gives the average number of slots used.

4. **[CLI] Read the same plan as JSON.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq ls -j -n 1
bq show --format=prettyjson -j &lt;JOB_ID&gt; | python3 -c "
import sys, json
j = json.load(sys.stdin)
for s in j['statistics']['query']['queryPlan']:
    print(s['name'], '| slot ms:', s.get('slotMs'), '| shuffle bytes:', s.get('shuffleOutputBytes'))"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Stages | Input → Join/Aggregate → Output |
| Hot stage | Largest slot time |
| Shuffle | Data moved between stages |
| Average slots | Slot ms ÷ elapsed ms |
